messages:
Asha (CSM): quick midweek check-in for MidCohort account — noticed a sudden spike in token throughput and a small latency blur. Putting numbers here so we can triage: WoW token usage +22% (last wk 1.95M -> 2.38M), QoQ +30%. Weekly spend jumped to ~$4.1k (up ~28%). p50 stable (~85ms) but p95 rose from 180ms -> 235ms. Error rate at 0.9% (recent 503s between 10:12-10:28 PT). Can we confirm root cause + any rollout impacts? @Ben (Platform Eng) any recent model variant changes or routing adjustments?

Ben (Platform Eng): saw the automated alert from healthbot. No intentional model rollouts on their account. I pulled the runtime logs — there's a pattern of KV cache evictions and a burst of long seq requests (seq>1024) around the same window. That increases mem pressure and causes queuing. Putting a quick log excerpt:
```
[2025-09-20T10:14:03Z] req_id=abc123 seq_len=1280 kv_cache_evicted=true gpu_mem=93% queue_time=42ms
[2025-09-20T10:15:10Z] req_id=abc457 seq_len=1408 kv_cache_evicted=true gpu_mem=95% err=503
```
I recommend temporarily tightening seq length caps for this account and enabling prefix caching for their most common prompt. Will follow up with a config change if folks agree.

Leo (CS Ops): :eyes: I can scope the prefix sets and show top prompt fingerprints. Also noticed their burst aligns with a scheduled nightly job from their infra that started new A/B tests last week. Nina, did they mention enabling larger context in the enablement call?

Nina (AE): they did mention experimenting with longer context for a pilot. I flagged that as an onboarding activity last week. Renewal is green but we should avoid bill shock; customer is sensitive to spend increases. I'll message them to pause the experiment if we ask for a quick rollback.

Asha (CSM): thanks. Action plan ideas:
- Ben: apply short-term seq cap (e.g., max_seq 1024) + enable prefix caching (owner: Ben, ETA 30m)
- Leo: compile top 10 prompts/contexts and confirm which ones to cache (owner: Leo, ETA 2h)
- Nina: ask customer to pause the A/B longer-context experiment and mention we're investigating (owner: Nina, ETA 1h)
- Opsbot: correlate cost attribution across the spike (owner: healthbot)

Ben (Platform Eng): applying the cap now on a canary route for this account. Command I'm running:
```
redwoodctl route update --account midcohort --max-seq 1024 --enable-prefix-cache
```
I'll watch p95 and error rate for the next 30m.

healthbot: automated alert summary: account=MidCohort window=2025-09-20T10:10-10:30 PT tokens=425k (burst) p95_before=180ms p95_peak=238ms errors=28(0.9%) estimated_cost_impact=$1.1k

Leo (CS Ops): pulled top prompt fingerprints — 3 templates account for ~68% of the burst. Will share a small list in the ticket. :thumbsup:

Ben (Platform Eng): canary results after 15m: p95 down to 190ms, error rate dropped to 0.25%. No regressions seen. Rolling change to primary route in 10m if stable.

Asha (CSM): excellent. Nina — if customer agrees to pause, we can keep the cap until they optimize prompts. Also want to schedule a short enablement session next Tue to show batching/cache wins.

Nina (AE): I'll ping them now. If they accept, we should highlight cost delta and request to postpone the pilot until after the enablement.

Asha (CSM): OK—tracking owners. Creating a ticket and adding the config diffs + logs: TKT-4627. I'll update renewal notes (low risk but monitor monthly spend trend). Thanks all. :raised_hands:

Ben (Platform Eng): FYI I'll add an opt-in quantization suggestion (from Optimize) for their embed-heavy route — could reduce token compute cost ~12% without model change.

Leo (CS Ops): adding follow-up: schedule a 30-min ops review with the customer next Tue 10am PT. Requesting CS + Eng + AE to join.

healthbot: ticket TKT-4627 created and linked to alert. Metrics dashboard snapshot: https://redwood.app/dashboards/TKT-4627/snapshot

Asha (CSM): will close loop after the meeting and check impact on next weekly health digest. Thx everyone. :raised_hands:
